title: Grade 5 French — Wed, Jun 11
description: La nourriture au marché — Day 3 of 5: Quantities and partitive articles
subject: french

questions.question: What is 'un kilo de' in English?
questions.explanation: 'Un kilo de' = a kilo of. 'Je voudrais un kilo de tomates.' = I would like a kilo of tomatoes.

questions.question: How do you say 'a litre of milk' in French?
questions.explanation: 'Un litre de lait' = a litre of milk. 'Je voudrais un litre de lait.' = I would like a litre of milk.

questions.question: What is 'une bouteille d'eau' in English?
questions.explanation: 'Une bouteille d'eau' = a bottle of water. 'Je bois une bouteille d'eau par jour.' = I drink a bottle of water per day.

questions.question: How do you say 'a dozen eggs' in French?
questions.explanation: 'Une douzaine d'œufs' = a dozen eggs. 'Douzaine' = dozen (12). 'Je voudrais une douzaine d'œufs.' = I would like a dozen eggs.

questions.question: What does 'du' mean when you say 'Je mange du pain'?
questions.explanation: 'Du' = 'de + le' = some (partitive article for masculine nouns). 'Je mange du pain.' = I eat some bread. 'Du' is used for uncountable things.

questions.question: What is 'de la' in 'Je bois de la limonade'?
questions.explanation: 'De la' = some (partitive article for feminine nouns). 'Je bois de la limonade.' = I drink some lemonade. Compare: 'du' (masculine) vs 'de la' (feminine).

questions.question: How do you say 'a packet of biscuits' in French?
questions.explanation: 'Un paquet de biscuits' = a packet of biscuits. 'Je voudrais un paquet de biscuits.' = I would like a packet of biscuits.

questions.question: After a negative (ne…pas), partitive articles change. 'Je mange du pain' (positive) → 'Je ne mange ___ pain.' (negative):
questions.explanation: After negation, 'du/de la/des' → 'de' (no article). 'Je ne mange pas de pain.' = I don't eat bread. This is a key French rule!

questions.question: How do you say 'a bag of flour' in French?
questions.explanation: 'Un sac de farine' = a bag of flour. 'Farine' = flour. 'La boulangère achète un sac de farine.' = The baker buys a bag of flour.

questions.question: Complete the shopping list: '___ de pommes, ___ de lait, ___ d'œufs.'
options: Un litre / une bouteille / un kilo
Deux kilos / un litre / une douzaine
questions.explanation: A natural shopping list: 'Deux kilos de pommes, un litre de lait, une douzaine d'œufs.' = Two kilos of apples, a litre of milk, a dozen eggs.

questions.question: Translate: 'I would like half a kilo of tomatoes.'
options: Je voudrais un kilo de tomates.
Je voudrais un demi-kilo de tomates.
Je voudrais deux kilos de tomates.
questions.explanation: 'Je voudrais un demi-kilo de tomates.' = I would like half a kilo of tomatoes. 'Un demi-kilo' = half a kilo.

questions.question: How do you ask 'How much does a kilo of mangoes cost?' in French?
options: C'est combien, un kilo de mangues?
Où est le kilo de mangues?
Je voudrais un kilo de mangues.
questions.explanation: 'C'est combien, un kilo de mangues?' = How much does a kilo of mangoes cost? 'C'est combien?' = How much is it/does it cost?

questions.question: Which phrase correctly says 'some vegetables' in French?
questions.explanation: 'Des légumes' = some vegetables. 'Des' is the partitive/indefinite plural — used when talking about an unspecified amount of a plural noun.

questions.question: Complete: 'Je n'ai pas ___ sucre.' (I don't have any sugar.)
questions.explanation: After 'pas', use 'de' (not 'du'). 'Je n'ai pas de sucre.' = I don't have any sugar. Partitive articles after negation → always 'de'.

questions.question: Arrange a market dialogue: A says '___'; B says '___'.
options: Bonjour! / Je voudrais deux kilos de pommes, s'il vous plaît.
All three dialogues together make a complete market exchange.
questions.explanation: A complete market exchange: 'Bonjour! / Je voudrais deux kilos de pommes, s'il vous plaît. / C'est cinq euros. / Voilà, merci!' = Hello! / I'd like two kilos of apples, please. / That's five euros. / Here you are, thank you!
